hypothesis: Combining heterogeneous detectors (classical forensics, deep learning, and non-visual signals such as metadata) via calibrated score-level and decision-level fusion yields higher robustness to watermark removal attacks—measured by improved ROC-AUC, attack-conditioned recall at fixed false positive rate, and robustness under distribution shift—than any single detector alone, under comparable latency and resource budgets.

baseline.description: Best-performing single-modality, single-model detectors from earlier chapters, evaluated independently on identical inputs.

detectors.expected_behavior: Predicts probability that an image has undergone watermark removal, using raw pixels (optionally with forensic pre-processing) as input.
Predicts watermark removal probability using handcrafted forensic features and a classical ML classifier (e.g., SVM or gradient-boosted trees).
Predicts watermark removal probability for a video segment based on temporal consistency anomalies across frames.
Predicts likelihood of watermark removal using metadata and coarse behavioral/contextual signals (no pixels).

baseline.evaluation_mode: Each baseline is evaluated separately; no cross-detector fusion. For multimodal inputs (e.g., video + metadata), baselines still use only their native modality.

treatment.description: Multimodal, ensemble-based detectors that combine outputs from baseline detectors and auxiliary signals via calibrated score fusion, stacking, and tiered decision rules.

details.feature_extraction: Use penultimate-layer embedding from baseline_img_deep concatenated with normalized handcrafted forensic feature vector from baseline_img_forensics.
details.meta_model: 2–3 layer MLP classifier trained on concatenated features with cross-entropy loss.
details.training_protocol: Train on train split only, with 5-fold CV on validation portion to choose MLP capacity and regularization.

details.calibration: Apply Platt scaling or isotonic regression per detector on validation data to map scores to calibrated probabilities.
details.weight_selection: Optimize detector weights (w_deep, w_forensics) on validation set to maximize ROC-AUC or detection cost function.
details.final_score: p_ensemble = w_deep * p_deep + w_forensics * p_forensics, with w_deep + w_forensics = 1.

details.level1_features: Calibrated probabilities and optional uncertainty measures (e.g., entropy) from each component model, plus key risk-sensitive metadata features (e.g., missing expected provenance tag, suspicious edit history).
details.meta_model: Logistic regression or gradient-boosted trees predicting final watermark-removal probability.
details.cv_protocol: Use K-fold cross-validation on training split to produce out-of-fold predictions for meta-model training, avoiding target leakage.

details.tier1: Cheap metadata_behavior and downsampled frame-level deep detector (baseline_img_deep on 1–3 keyframes). Route obviously benign or obviously malicious samples to 'safe auto-decision' bucket.
details.tier2: For ambiguous cases, run full video_temporal model on a subset of frames and classical forensic features for those frames.
details.decision_aggregation: Combine per-frame and per-model scores via calibrated weighted fusion; expose uncertainty score. Provide interpretable rationale (which tier, which signal dominated).

workloads.description: Image-level watermark-removal detection on the main test set drawn from the same distribution as Chapters 4–6 (standard watermarks, standard removal attacks).

constraints.class_balance: Approximately balanced between clean, watermarked_not_removed, and watermarked_then_removed.

workloads.description: Image-level detection under distribution shift: new content domains and unseen or more aggressive removal attacks.
Video-level watermark-removal detection with multiple modalities: video frames, temporal features, and metadata/behavioral context.
Case-study workload simulating a media platform’s tiered pipeline with realistic ingestion patterns and latency budgets.

data_splits.protocol: Train/validation/test splits fixed and shared with earlier chapters where applicable.
data_splits.leakage_prevention: No image/video or near-duplicate should appear in both train and test; use perceptual hashing to de-duplicate.

preprocessing.image_normalization: Resize to common size (e.g., 256x256) with center crop or preserve aspect via padding; normalize channels to ImageNet statistics for deep models.
preprocessing.video_sampling: For video workloads, sample frames at a fixed rate (e.g., 4 fps) and limit to max_frames_per_video; ensure identical sampling for all detectors in comparison.
preprocessing.metadata_sanitization: Standardize metadata fields (e.g., missing to NULL, categorical encodings) and redact PII in the experimental dataset.

model_freeze_policy.baseline_models: Weights frozen; no retraining beyond calibration steps.
model_freeze_policy.treatment_ensembles: Only ensemble meta-models and fusion weights are trained; underlying detectors remain frozen to isolate ensemble effects.

evaluation_protocol.confidence_intervals: Compute 95% bootstrap CIs for key metrics on test sets.
evaluation_protocol.stratification: Report metrics stratified by attack family and content category (e.g., photography vs. illustration).

governance_safeguards.dual_use_mitigation: Attack scripts are reused from Chapter 8; no new more powerful removal attacks developed here.
governance_safeguards.access_control: Sensitive behavioral features (if any) simulated or anonymized; clearly documented in dataset cards.

metrics.name: roc_auc
metrics.description: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for the binary task 'watermark_removed' vs 'clean_or_watermarked_intact'.

metrics.name: pr_auc_positive_removed
metrics.description: Area under the precision–recall curve where the positive class is 'watermark_removed'.

metrics.name: recall_at_fpr_1pct
metrics.description: Recall (true positive rate) at a fixed false positive rate of 1% for the 'watermark_removed' class.

metrics.name: recall_per_attack_family_at_fpr_1pct
metrics.description: Recall at 1% overall FPR, computed separately for each attack type (e.g., jpeg_recompression, diffusion_resynthesis_standard).

metrics.name: brier_score
metrics.description: Mean squared error between predicted probabilities and binary labels, used as a measure of calibration quality.

metrics.name: ece_10bin
metrics.description: Expected calibration error using 10 equal-width probability bins.

metrics.name: throughput_qps
metrics.description: Effective detection throughput measured under workload wl_operational_tiered_case_study.

metrics.name: latency_p95_ms
metrics.description: 95th percentile end-to-end detection latency per item (image or video) including all tiers.

metrics.name: latency_p99_ms
metrics.description: 99th percentile end-to-end detection latency per item (image or video) including all tiers.

metrics.name: compute_cost_normalized
metrics.description: Approximate per-item compute cost normalized so that the baseline_img_deep cost on wl_image_in_distribution equals 1.0.

metrics.name: explainability_proxy_score
metrics.description: Heuristic measure reflecting fraction of decisions accompanied by simple, human-readable rationales (e.g., dominant signal and tier), as a proxy for explainability.

primary.description: On image in-distribution workload (wl_image_in_distribution), the best-performing image ensemble (treat_early_fusion_img or treat_score_fusion_img) must outperform the best single image baseline (max over baseline_img_deep and baseline_img_forensics) by at least 0.02 absolute ROC-AUC with non-overlapping 95% bootstrap CIs.

On shifted image workload (wl_image_shifted), the stacking ensemble with metadata (treat_stacking_img_meta) must improve recall_at_fpr_1pct for watermarked_removed by at least 0.05 absolute compared to baseline_img_deep and baseline_img_forensics, when averaged over seeds.

On video multimodal workload (wl_video_multimodal), the tiered pipeline (treat_multimodal_video_pipeline) must achieve higher recall_per_attack_family_at_fpr_1pct than baseline_video_temporal on at least 70% of attack families, without reducing overall roc_auc.

secondary.description: On wl_operational_tiered_case_study, the tiered pipeline (treat_multimodal_video_pipeline) must meet latency and throughput targets (p95_latency_ms <= 250, p99_latency_ms <= 500, throughput_qps >= 50) with compute_cost_normalized <= 2.0.

Ensembles that include metadata (treat_stacking_img_meta, treat_multimodal_video_pipeline) must not materially degrade calibration (brier_score and ece_10bin) relative to best baseline; allowable degradation is <= 0.01 absolute.

Explainability proxy score for the tiered pipeline (treat_multimodal_video_pipeline) must be >= 0.8, indicating that at least 80% of decisions come with simple textual rationales (e.g., 'Tier2: high forensic anomaly in DCT band; metadata missing expected provenance flag').

failure_modes.description: Stacked and early-fusion ensembles overfit validation data, yielding improved metrics on wl_image_in_distribution but no gains or regressions on wl_image_shifted and wl_video_multimodal.
failure_modes.detection: Compare in-distribution vs. shifted performance deltas; high variance across seeds or attack families suggests overfitting.
mitigations: Use stricter regularization or simpler meta-models (e.g., logistic regression instead of deep MLP).
Increase size and diversity of training split for ensembles using cross-domain samples.

failure_modes.description: Metadata features encode dataset-specific artifacts (e.g., file naming conventions) that leak label information, artificially inflating ensemble performance.
failure_modes.detection: Ablate visual signals and evaluate metadata-only model; unusually high performance or strong split-by-dataset effects indicate leakage.
mitigations: Drop or randomize suspicious metadata fields.
Rebalance or re-split data so that such artifacts do not correlate with labels.

failure_modes.description: Tiered pipeline incurs excessive latency for ambiguous cases, violating p95/p99 latency budgets under wl_operational_tiered_case_study.
failure_modes.detection: Monitor per-tier latency distributions; identify tiers or models causing most delay.
mitigations: Adjust routing thresholds to reduce the proportion of items reaching the most expensive tier.
Optimize or prune heavy models; reduce frame sampling density.

failure_modes.description: Calibrated score-fusion weights vary greatly across seeds, leading to unstable deployment behavior.
failure_modes.detection: Analyze distribution of learned weights over multiple calibration runs; large variance implies instability.
mitigations: Constrain weights with priors (e.g., Dirichlet) or regularization.
Use fixed, heuristically chosen weights validated across multiple datasets.

failure_modes.description: Explainability proxy is low or rationales contradict quantitative signals (e.g., rationale cites metadata, but metadata score was low).
failure_modes.detection: Sanity-check sample rationales against logged component scores in evidence records.
mitigations: Implement deterministic rule-based rationale generation based on thresholds over component scores.
Add unit tests to ensure rationale text matches underlying numeric decisions.

Install dependencies: pip install -r requirements.txt OR use provided environment.yml with conda.
Run basic tests: pytest -q OR provided smoke-test script (e.g., scripts/run_smoke_tests.sh).

determinism_flags: Configure torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic=True and benchmark=False if using PyTorch.
Document any non-deterministic operations (e.g., certain CUDA kernels).

evidence_schema.description: Canonical JSON structure for recording per-run, per-model, and per-workload evidence for Chapter 10 experiments. All evaluation scripts must emit data conforming to this schema to support reproducibility, auditing, and downstream reporting.

models.description: List of models evaluated in this run, including baselines and ensembles.

config_hash.description: Short hash (e.g., SHA256 truncated) of the model configuration file for traceability.
